title: Input-output Conformance Testing for Channel-based Service Connectors
review_status: full-text audit complete; formal model and illustrative conformance tests, no deployment-scale validation
sections_checked: Reo constraint automata and mCRL2 translation
ioco testing relation and test generation
worked correct/incorrect connector examples
JTorX/tool-support discussion
conclusion and stated implementation/scaling limitations
venue_year_verified: arXiv v1 submitted 2011-08-09; EPTCS 60 (2011), pp. 19-35, DOI 10.4204/EPTCS.60.2.
evidence_note: Maps Reo models to mCRL2/LTS and reuses ioco/JTorX to distinguish example connector implementations. The paper says BPEL-to-Reo-to-mCRL2 correctness depends on semantics-preserving translations; an adapter to the distributed Java implementation was ongoing. Compositional scalability is an expectation, not a measured large-system result. Demonstrative formal evidence, not operational fault-yield evidence.

title: Semantics-based Automated Web Testing
review_status: full-text audit complete; empirical evidence bounded to arithmetic examples and one parking-calculator site
sections_checked: TAO grammar and semantic-oracle architecture
grammar-directed delta-debugging algorithms
five buggy Java arithmetic programs and Tables 1-2
Selenium parking calculator setup and 500-script result
200-script reduction study, reported faults, and conclusion
venue_year_verified: arXiv v1 submitted 2015-08-17; EPTCS 188 (2015), pp. 59-74, DOI 10.4204/EPTCS.188.7.
evidence_note: Five buggy Java programs: 1,000 generated expressions and 81% mean failing-input length reduction. One airport parking calculator: 500 generated JUnit scripts, reported 11.24% average failure ratio; in a 200-executable-script reduction set 28 failed and GDD reduced failing scripts by 22% on average. Single-site/manual grammar and semantics; failure ratio is not independently validated defect prevalence and cross-site transfer is untested.

title: Disentangling Flaws in Linux DCTCP
review_status: full-text audit complete; controlled network experiments and implementation-level causal diagnosis, deployment impact unresolved
sections_checked: experimental design and variant matrix
Linux PRR/RFC 6937 discrepancy and TSO interaction
patch behavior in data-center and WAN setups
post-fix latecomer-fairness issue and alpha toggle results
AQM marking alternatives, appendices, and limitations
evidence_note: Controlled experiments connect a Linux PRR/RFC discrepancy plus TSO deferral to stalls, bursts, and under-utilization; aligning code with RFC resolves that symptom in shown configurations but unmasks latecomer fairness. Removing an alpha toggle can improve selected steady-state utilization while worsening competition equilibria/CCA behavior. Authors say realistic production impact remains unknown; results depend on implementation and testbed settings.

title: Can LLMs Recover Program Semantics? A Systematic Evaluation with Symbolic Execution
review_status: full-text audit complete; mixed model/transformation effects and proxy semantic metric, not strict equivalence validation
sections_checked: RQ and metric definitions
dataset selection and filtering
model/training setup
compilation and semantic score tables by transformation
readability results, limitations, and claims versus tables
evidence_note: 170 C programs × four obfuscation transforms. Body tables contradict a universal reading of abstract-level consistent gains: base GPT arithmetic compilation is 75.8% with KLEE versus 93.9% without, while Codestral arithmetic semantic score is 51.17 versus 54.59; effects vary by model/transformation. Semantic score is based on KLEE test/path-count similarity, not a strict equivalence proof. Path-explosion/context-size filtering limits the evaluated population.
